title: Request For Quote - DART-Mass Spectrometer
description: Request for Quote (RFQ) � 192126VHQFDL00016 DART-Mass Spectrometer 1. Point of Contact: Chris Jackson, 8222 N. Belt Line Road, Irving, Texas 75063 Questions: All questins shall be submitted no later than 1:00 pm, Eastern Time, Thursday, September 17, 2026. Email quotes to: Christopher.L.Jackson@ice.dhs.gov by 0800, Eastern, September 23, 2026. Basis for Award: The Government intends to evaluate quotes in response to this RFQ using the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) process. Quotes shall be evaluated in order of total price (lowest price first) until a technically acceptable quote is determined. Quotes will be evaluated for acceptability only. A quote shall be determined to be technically acceptable or unacceptable based on the rating definitions in the table below. The technically acceptable quote will then have its price evaluated for reasonableness. All quotes may not be evaluated at the Government�s discretion. Rating Definitions: Acceptable The quotation meets and/or exceed the minimim specifications as listed below. Unacceptable The quotation does not meet the minimum specifications as listed below. . 2. Set Aside: None 3. NAICS: 334516 PSC: 6640 4. Description: The Government would like to purchase a Direct Analysis in Real-Time Mass Spectrometer (DART-MS) that will fulfill the HSI Forensics Laboratory mission to perform rapid, non-destructive mass spectral analyses of inks, toners, dyes, polymers, papers, adhesives, and other materials related to travel, identity, and security documents. The DART source must be capable of rapid qualitative and quantitative analysis with no sample preparation of a wide range of polar and nonpolar materials including polymers and polymer additives, fuel additives, drugs and metabolites (either purified or in body fluids or tissues), explosives, foods and beverages, environmental contaminants, pesticides, and chemical warfare agents. The DART system must be controlled through the software provided. The DART must be a fully integrated (with the MS and software) and be a commercially available instrument that has previously been sold and installed into US Federal and State government laboratories, industrial and pharmaceutical companies, as well as universities and colleges The DART-MS equipment must meet the following minimum requirements listed below: -TAA compliant - Must include DART JumpShot: DART JumpShot with Pulse gas flow is an easy way to complete ambient pressure desorption ionization mass spectrometry. JumpShot technology improves speed and throughput, reduces ambient background and allows for 95% helium saving over continuous flow DART. All hardware required for operation of the DART-MS instrument � PC (and related peripherals that meets or exceeds the following specifications: Intel Core i5-13600 with Windows 11� Pro or Mac OSX 64-bit Operating System, Minimum of 16GB RAM, 256GB SSD & 4TB SATA disk drives, 24" flat panel monitor optical mouse, keyboard, and all necessary cables Includes accessory pumps, gas regulator(s), etc. The Mass spectrometer must meet or exceed the following specifications: Time-of-flight mass spectrometer including ESI ion source, DART ion source, isolation valve, ion transmission guide, ion accelerator, analyzer, ion detection unit, ADC system, evacuation and control system. Syringe pump for system tuning. Positive and Negative ion detection No special interface or pump required for using DART Resolving Power: greater than or equal to 10,000 (FWHM) at m/z 609 Data Acquisition Rate: up to 50Hz Mass Range of at least: m/z 7-10,000 Mass Accuracy: 3ppm (RMS) or better Supports up to multiple in-source CID voltages for a single analysis Vacuum isolation valve permits rapid pump down after venting the ion source region for maintenance Must be capable of using Helium and Nitrogen gas as a carrier gas High-Resolution, capable of exact mass and true isotopic pattern measurements Data from analyses can be matched against database spectra measured from other models of DART-MS, including but not limited to the NIST DART Forensic Database, and the US Fish and Wildlife Forensic Laboratory wood database. Atmospheric pressure interface is user serviceable. Is a non-contact source that does not require that the sample be prepared in solvent or reside in a vacuum. The DART source can analyze vapors, solids, and liquid sample types MS is fully integrated with the direct analysis in real time (DART) source. A single software controls both the DART sample introduction and MS detector. The DART source does not use radiation and does not expose the sample to high voltages Capable of detecting masses as low as 7Li+ and atmospheric ions from m/z 15 and higher. Meets or exceeds spectral storage rate of at least 40 spectra per second at a resolving power in excess of 10,000 (FWHM definition). Can be shutdown and restarted routinely without detrimental effects to the instrument performance. can measure molecular ions, even for difficult nonpolar compounds such as saturated alkanes. Supports the use of optional ion sources such as atmospheric pressure ionization (APCI), nanoelectrospray (nanoESI), CoronaSpray, PaperSpray� and DualSpray. Data interpretation and reporting software is provided that includes: elemental composition determination functions integrated searching of NIST-formatted mass spectral databases and on-line chemical databases for compounds with elemental compositions matching those calculated by the software. chemometric analysis should include principal component analysis (PCA) and kernel PCA, linear and kernel discriminant analysis (LDA and KDA), partial least squares (PLS), support vector machine (SVM), Fisher ratio analysis and heat maps. Heat maps can be exported to third-party software for hierarchical cluster analysis. Kendrick mass defect analysis including nontraditional and 3D Kendrick mass defect plots target compound identification and report generation support for creation of custom mass spectral databases/libraries modeling of overlapping isotopic distributions at any arbitrary resolving power Ion series analysis database searching including correlation and matching of mass spectra acquired with different collision energies with post-search exact-mass and elemental composition filters. The software is linked to databases such as NIST and Wiley mass spectral databases. fully off-line. Does not require internet/web connectivity for use of any function � database searching, data collection, analysis, or interpretation. can determine unique elemental compositions for unknown compounds by using isotopic exact masses and abundances. Provides information to support assignments for known or suspected compounds. The software to perform this assignment is provided.

buyer: UNITED STATES AGENCY FOR GLOBAL MEDIA, BBG
title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source-Medium Wave broadcasting services on the specific frequency of 864 kHz for Radio Farda
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT. This notice is issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) section 5.201 to notify the public of a proposed contract action. The North American Identification Classification System (NAICS) code is 516110 - Radio Broadcasting Stations The SBA size standard is_$47 Million Average Annual Receipts. The U.S Agency of Global Media (USAGM) intends to award a contract, on a sole source basis under the authority of FAR 6.302-1, to Global Emergency Media Ltd (GEMA) a radio broadcasting firm with its registered office at 20�22 Wenlock Road, London, England, N1 7GU . The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C.3304(a)(1) as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1, which reads in part, �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.� USAGM requires Medium Wave broadcasting services on the specific frequency of 864 kHz for Radio Farda, a service of Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL), to provide programming to audiences in Iran. The Office of Technology, Services, and Innovation (TSI) requires uninterrupted continuation of these mission-critical broadcasting services. USAGM has determined that Global Emergency Media Ltd. (GEMA) is the only known source capable of meeting the Government's requirements without interruption to ongoing Radio Farda broadcasts and associated support services. The required transmission facilities provide effective Medium Wave coverage into Iran from a geographically advantageous location. Use of the existing broadcasting infrastructure is essential to maintaining uninterrupted delivery of programming to the target audience. The Period of Performance will be date of award plus four months. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. A determination by the Government not to compete this procurement based on responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the Government. Interested parties who believe they possess the capability to satisfy this requirement should submit documentation that clearly demonstrates their capability. Responses to this notice shall be received no later than September 23, 2026 at 8AM EST. All responses must be in writing only via email to the point of contacts specified in this notice. Telephone requests or inquires will not be accepted. Any cost associated with the preparation and submission of data or information in response to this notice is the sole responsibility of the respondent and will not be reimbursed by the Government

The DART source does not use radiation and does not expose the sample to high voltages Capable of detecting masses as low as 7Li+ and atmospheric ions from m/z 15 and higher. Meets or exceeds spectral storage rate of at least 40 spectra per second at a resolving power in excess of 10,000 (FWHM definition). Can be shutdown and restarted routinely without detrimental effects to the instrument performance. can measure molecular ions, even for difficult nonpolar compounds such as saturated alkanes. Supports the use of optional ion sources such as atmospheric pressure ionization (APCI), nanoelectrospray (nanoESI), CoronaSpray, PaperSpray� and DualSpray. Data interpretation and reporting software is provided that includes: elemental composition determination functions integrated searching of NIST-formatted mass spectral databases and on-line chemical databases for compounds with elemental compositions matching those calculated by the software. chemometric analysis should include principal component analysis (PCA) and kernel PCA, linear and kernel discriminant analysis (LDA and KDA), partial least squares (PLS), support vector machine (SVM), Fisher ratio analysis and heat maps. Heat maps can be exported to third-party software for hierarchical cluster analysis. Kendrick mass defect analysis including nontraditional and 3D Kendrick mass defect plots target compound identification and report generation support for creation of custom mass spectral databases/libraries modeling of overlapping isotopic distributions at any arbitrary resolving power Ion series analysis database searching including correlation and matching of mass spectra acquired with different collision energies with post-search exact-mass and elemental composition filters. The software is linked to databases such as NIST and Wiley mass spectral databases. fully off-line. Does not require internet/web connectivity for use of any function � database searching, data collection, analysis, or interpretation. can determine unique elemental compositions for unknown compounds by using isotopic exact masses and abundances. Provides information to support assignments for known or suspected compounds. The software to perform this assignment is provided.

title: Schüchtermann-Klinik, Neubau Kardiologie Tischlerarbeiten - Innenwandbekleidung
description: Allgemein: Die Ausführung des fünften Bauabschnittes zum Neubau der Kardiologie der Schüchtermann-Klinik beinhaltet den Neubau des Gebäudeteils H als Erweiterung zum vorhandenen Gebäude. Die Schüchtermann-Klinik verbleibt während der gesamten Neubaumaßnahme in Betrieb, sodass hier erhöhte Anforderungen an den Emissionsschutz gestellt werden. Bei großflächiger Öffnung des vorhandenen Gebäudes sind ebenfalls die hauseigenen Hygienestandards zu beachten. Allgemeine Baubeschreibung: Bauteil H besteht aus einem L-förmigen Gebäudeflügel, der unmittelbar an ein in Funktion befindliches Krankenhausgebäude angrenzt. Der Gebäudeflügel besteht aus 2 Vollgeschossen (EG, 1. OG) und einem zurückgesetzten Staffelgeschoss (2. OG) sowie einem Untergeschoss. Baukonstruktion: Die tragenden und aussteifenden Bauteile einschließlich der Treppenhäuser und Aufzugsschächte werden aus Stahlbeton hergestellt. Die Deckenkonstruktion erfolgt in Massivbauweise. Tragende Wände bestehen aus Stahlbeton oder Kalksandstein. Nicht tragende Wände bestehen aus Trockenbau oder Kalksandstein. Zur Fassadengestaltung werden Einzelfenster aus Leichtmetallprofilen mit einer Verschattungsanlage verbaut. Zwischen den Fenstern sowie an den restlichen Fassadenflächen erfolgt eine Verkleidung aus Faserzementplatten. Auf den jeweiligen Etagen sind neben Akustikdecken, Gipsdecken, Metalldecken auch Putzflächen zur Ausführung vorgesehen. Die Bodenbeläge im Bereich der Treppenhäuser sollen aus Feinsteinzeug und in den übrigen Bereichen aus Polyvinylchlorid oder synthetischem Kautschuk bestehen.

title: France – Earthmoving work – Opération de Modernisation du Métro Fer (OMF19) - Modernisation L12 - Lot GC05 : Station Marx Dormoy – Elargissement de la trémie d’accès existante – Travaux de génie civil et d’aménagements
description: Les travaux visent à maitriser l’impact du nouveau matériel roulant (MF19) sur les dispositions de sécurité en améliorant les conditions d’évacuation afin d’atteindre le seuil réglementaire de 10min. Les travaux consistent à démolir le débouché DB202 (EF & EM) actuel et de reconstruire un débouché plus large avec la création d’un escalier mécanique côté rue de la chapelle et un escalier fixe plus large. Le chantier sera réalisé de jour excepté quelques tâches liées à l’installation des emprises de chantier. La pose des GBA pour l’immobilisation d’une voie de la rue de la Chapelle sera réalisée de nuit. Durant toute la période des travaux de déconstruction et reconstruction du débouché 202, la station Marx Dormoy sera fermée. Cependant, l’exploitation de la ligne 12 est maintenue durant les travaux et les trains ne marqueront pas l’arrêt à la station Marx Dormoy. Pour la réalisation des travaux du projet, la RATP mettra à disposition des locaux d’une surface de 165m² situés 28 rue de la Chapelle à Paris. Ces locaux feront office de base vie.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Metaphase Chromosome Harvesters
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) in Fort Detrick, MD intends to negotiate on a sole source basis (IAW RFO 12.102(a)) with ADS BIOTEC INC 5781 Van Allen Way, Carlsbad, CA 92008 as the only responsible source that can provide the delivery and installation of one (1) Card Processing Automation CPA200� instrument. This is a Presolicitation notice in accordance with RFO 5.101. The equipment provided by ADS BIOTEC INC is the only source that provides DHACA with the delivery and installation of two (2) Metaphase Chromosome Harvesters instrument. used at the Armed Forces Radiobiology Research Institute (AFRRI) to support their mission. AFRRI has been requested by the Defense Health Agency (DHA) to set up a multiple parameter biodosimetry network including the ability to assess radiation exposure using cytogenetic biodosimetry. Typically, blood samples are received by the Cytogenetic Biodosimetry Laboratory, and a blood culture is set up for a 48-h incubation at 37? 37oC where lymphocytes are stimulated to divide using a mitogen. The harvest of these 48-h culture involves a series of laborious steps including: a) centrifugation to pellet cells, b) aspiration of the supernatant, c) addition of hypotonic solution to cell to lysis RBCs for a define time, c) vortexing to mix cultures, d) repeated centrifugation to pellet cells, e) aspiration of the supernatant, f) addition of Carnoy Solution to wash cells g) vortexing of the samples, h) centrifugation of the solution, i) aspiration of the supernatant, and repeating twice again steps g, h, and I for multiple culture samples. These manual steps typically take approximately 2 h. This acquisition is being conducted under simplified acquisition procedures. There are no set-aside restrictions for this requirement. The intended procurement will be classified under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 334516 with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,000 employees. This presolicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation document exists for this requirement. However, any parties interested in responding to this notice shall submit technical data, including cost, sufficient to determine capability in providing the same service. All capability statements received by closing of this notification of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Based on the above information, the only technically acceptable subscription can be provided by ADS BIOTEC INC . Submit email capability statements (using PDF, MS Word, Excel attachments) to Alicia Maldonado Torres at alicia.maldonadotorres.civ@health.mil. Statements are due no later than 9:00 A.M. EST on 23 August 2026. No phone calls will be accepted.

The scope of the project also includes a reflection on the interior design of the entire building as well as the turnkey development of certain exterior signage elements. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE The period of the Contract is from date of Contract to August 15, 2027 inclusive. Bidders should provide, in writing, to the Contracting Authority, the name(s) of the person(s) who will be attending and a list of issues they wish to table no later than September 7, 2026 at 2:00 PM. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the bidders' conference will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. Bidders who do not attend will not be precluded from submitting a bid. LANGUAGE REQUIREMENTS The Parks Canada Agency has an obligation to respect the spirit and letter of the Official Languages Act, R.S. 1985, c. 31 (4th Supp.). Written communications will be in the recipients' language(s) and must be forwarded to the Project Authority before being sent. If the intervening participants need to communicate with the consultant or its representatives by telephone, the consultant must ensure that all persons, including receptionists and other key people who receive these calls, are bilingual ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) calendar days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Procurement Office: The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Yuma Proving Ground (MICC-YPG), is currently conducting market research to bolster Government and industry coordination and partnership in support of the Department of Information Management (DoIM) at the United States Army Yuma Proving Ground (USAYPG), Arizona. This RFI is being issued to inquire about industry capability to provide critical power and cooling support services for the YPG data center. A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is provided as an attachment. Respondents are strongly encouraged to provide thorough answers to all questions outlined in this RFI and to explicitly address the relevant sections of the PWS within their submissions. Information Sought: (1) Has your company delivered services outlined in the PWS under Part 5, Specific Tasks? If applicable, please provide: Contract number or customer name Total contract value Period of performance Brief synopsis of the scope of the work performed (2) Is your company capable of providing the services described in the attached draft PWS? If yes, please describe your company�s capability to perform this requirement. (3) Is your company interested in competing for this requirement as a prime contractor? If not, would your company be interested as a subcontractor? (4) Does your company believe this requirement is a commercial service as defined in FAR 2.101? If not, please explain. (5) Does industry agree that the use of NAICS code 541513, Computer Facilities Management Services, is the best fit for this requirement? If not, please suggest an alternative and explain why. (6) What is your firm�s size and status under NAICS 541513? Please identify whether your firm is a small business and any applicable socioeconomic category or contract vehicle. (7) If your company cannot perform this requirement, please identify the primary reasons why. THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. This is not a Request for Quote (RFQ), and the Government is not seeking quotes at this time. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Responses to this notice will be used for market research purposes only. The Government is interested in input from the small business community, as well as other interested sources, regarding their capability to meet the requirement. Small businesses in all socioeconomic categories are encouraged to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement. INFORMATION: The proposed requirement is anticipated to be classified under NAICS 541513, Computer Facilities Management Services. This NAICS was selected because it includes establishments primarily engaged in providing on site management, operation, and support services for clients� computer systems and/or data processing facilities. The applicable small business size standard for NAICS 541513 is $37M. Attachment: Draft PWS

title: V--International Expedited Freight Forwarding Service
description: Posted Date: September 8, 2026 Procurement Office: The Department of the Interior (DOI) � Interior Business Center (IBC), Acquisition Services Directorate (AQD) Response Due Date: September 23, 2026, at 1000 AM EST NOTICE OF INTENT SYNOPSIS: The DOI, IBC, AQD on behalf of Peace Corps� Office of Operations & Security intends to award three Contracts to Cavalier, EWC, and DBA, on a sole source basis for International Expedited Freight Forwarding Services. These Contracts are anticipated to include a 12-month base period and four 12-month Option Periods. The intended procurement is classified under North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) Code 488510 � Freight Transportation Arrangement. This is a Sole Source procurement under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12 � Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. There are only three responsible sources, and no other services will satisfy agency requirements. Description of Requirement: The Peace Corps Office of Operations & Security (Facilities Management Division) requires specialized international 4PL freight-forwarding, logistics, and customs-brokerage services for shipments originating from Peace Corps Headquarters to overseas Peace Corps posts in more than 60 countries. This requirement directly supports Volunteer health, safety, and operational infrastructure. Primary shipment categories include: � Temperature-Sensitive Medical Logistics: Pharmaceuticals, vaccines, biological materials, and prescription medications requiring continuous temperature maintenance (+2�C to +8�C, -20�C, and -80�C). � Dangerous Goods: IATA Class 9 hazardous materials, including non-removable lithium-ion batteries installed in IT and medical diagnostic units. � Diplomatic Cargo: Cargo requiring U.S. Department of State (DoS) Government Bills of Lading (GBL) and handoff into diplomatic pouch/cargo chains of custody. Peace Corps operating experience, shipping procedures, and market research to date � including review of vendor corporate history, public regulatory filings, and documented service capabilities � demonstrate that standard commercial parcel services do not provide the combined capability required for this requirement, particularly active cold-chain recovery during transit disruptions, specialized pharmaceutical customs support, and integration with Department of State diplomatic freight processes. Market research and Peace Corps operating experience identify three proposed sources as providing distinct capabilities relevant to the Government's minimum need: Cavalier Logistics, Expedited World Cargo (EWC), and Distribution by Air (DBA)/Radiant Logistics. Therefore, this requirement will be established as three BPAs, one each set up as a sole source to each of these vendors, based on the following rationale: � Common couriers do not offer end-to-end active cold-chain custody, in-transit dry-ice replenishment, or re-icing during flight interruptions or customs holds. In addition, standard commercial couriers generally leave destination customs clearance to the receiving Post. At many Posts, staff do not have the specialized brokerage relationships, pharmaceutical import expertise, or regulatory infrastructure necessary to resolve complex Ministry of Health and customs requirements within the validated cold-chain hold period. Failure to maintain temperature control during transit disruptions results in irreversible product excursion, complete inventory loss, and mission failure through delayed medical treatment for Volunteers. � Cavalier is the only source presently documented as providing this complete logistics model. Under Peace Corps' established cold-chain procedure, the Government maintains the required temperature only through the domestic transfer to Cavalier's Sterling, Virginia operation, after which Cavalier assumes responsibility for maintaining the temperature-controlled environment throughout the international movement, including access to temperature-controlled holding and the ability to restore the shipment's validated temperature-control configuration when necessary. Peace Corps' shipping decision matrix places Cavalier as the primary option for seasonal and short-expiry cold-chain shipments, with EWC identified only as a conditional alternative when the receiving Post is reachable and the applicable service guarantee is adequate, and the matrix specifically notes Cavalier's replacement guarantee. � EWC's primary differentiating value is customs, regulatory compliance, and difficult-destination logistics. Its in-house customs brokerage, government and Embassy experience, dangerous-goods capability, and international agent network provide an independent solution for shipments in which destination clearance, import regulations, or local logistics conditions present the principal operational risk. EWC's government/embassy role is distinct from DBA's: EWC's specialization addresses destination-side customs and regulatory clearance � navigating host-nation import requirements and difficult or post-conflict markets � rather than DBA's defense-credentialed secure packaging and transport function. � DBA's specialized value to Peace Corps is hazardous-material transportation and secure Government freight rather than active pharmaceutical cold-chain logistics. DBA's extensive dangerous-goods experience, federal transportation credentials, military/government freight expertise, and access to the broader Radiant carrier network provide an independent capability for Class 9 and other regulated shipments where airline acceptance, routing restrictions, carrier capacity, or destination conditions constrain ordinary transportation options. DBA holds a documented federal credential portfolio � including ITAR registration, DoD-approved carrier status, Civil Reserve Air Fleet carrier designation, AECA compliance, C-TPAT certification, and GSA-approved Transportation Service Provider status � supporting military-spec cargo packaging and secure transport of State Department-regulated cargo (e.g., gas detectors, lithium-battery equipment, and other non-cold-chain HAZMAT). In summation, Cavalier provides the Agency's sole documented full active cold-chain and diplomatic-integration capability for the most technically demanding shipments. DBA and EWC each provide independent, non-overlapping specialized networks � secure defense-credentialed transport and destination-side customs/compliance clearance, respectively � reducing the operational risk associated with dependence on a single international logistics network in a volatile global transit environment. Period of Performance: One 12-month Base Period and four 12-month Option Periods. Response Information: This action is being processed in accordance with 41U.S.C 1901 as implemented by RFO 12.102(b). title: Ireland – Laboratory services – Sampling and Analysis of Private Water Supplies in County Wexford
description: As the Supervisory authority for small private regulated water supplies in Wexford, Wexford County Council is required to monitor certain group water schemes and private premises which have their own wells, including caravan parks, schools, estates etc. The drinking water is sampled and analysed in accordance with S.l. No. 99/2023 - European Union (Drinking Water) Regulations 2023. Results are reported to Wexford County Council each month. The current compliance sampling contract ends on December 31st, 2026, and Wexford County Council is requesting tenders from interested parties for provision of these services. The service provider will be required to provide the following services: a) Compliance (and occasional investigative) sampling and analysis of drinking water for both 'check' and 'audit' parameters as set down by S.I. No. 99/2023 - European Union (Drinking Water) Regulations 2023 and listed in Appendix 1 Requirements and specifications. b) Occasional investigative sampling. These are normally duplicate samples i.e coliforms, e.coli free and total chlorine. Other parameters may also be asked for. c) In accordance with EPA requirements, all analysis of parameters in compliance samples (except for free and total chlorine, odour and taste and Dalapon) shall be accredited. Investigative samples do not have to be accredited. d) Reporting of results to Wexford County Council as detailed in Appendix 1 Requirements and specifications. There are currently about 170 private and group water supplies (Entities). This number is variable. It is expected that up to 15 additional schemes will be added during 2026 and these additional entities shall be sampled and analysed at tender rates. Each scheme shall have two check samples carried out annually. A small number of schemes will have more than two check samples and/or will require an audit sample. The level of analysis, including Limits of Detections must meet the requirements cited in S.I. No. 99/2023 - European Union (Drinking Water) Regulations 2023. The laboratory appointed (and/or sub contracted laboratory) must be accredited to !NAB (or equivalent) for all relevant parameters.

title: RFI/Sources Sought Notice, Heterotrophic Plate Count (HPC) Waterline Testing Services, Biloxi, MS, Pensacola, FL and Panama City Beach, FL
description: 1. PURPOSE The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is conducting market research to identify qualified and interested firms capable of providing routine and surge Heterotrophic Plate Count (HPC) testing of potable waterlines at VA facilities along the Gulf Coast. The Government seeks capability statements from Small Businesses (including SDVOSB/VOSB) and other than small businesses, and from GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) holders under SIN 541380 (Testing Laboratory Services). This RFI/Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not obligate the Government to award a contract. 2. BACKGROUND & REGULATORY CONTEXT HPC (Standard Methods 9215) estimates live culturable heterotrophic microorganisms in water and is used to monitor premise plumbing microbiological condition; consistent method/media selection is essential to preserve trend comparability. Short, strict hold times for HPC samples require reliable local logistics (cooling/transport and initiation of analysis within program limits�commonly ?24 hours, and in some jurisdictions ?8 hours for compliance). In healthcare settings, CDC expects facilities to operate comprehensive water management programs; EPA notes HPC can indicate general distribution-system water quality status, and ?500 CFU/mL is used for disinfectant-residual equivalency under SWTR. 3. DRAFT SCOPE OF WORK (SUMMARY) 3.1 Methods Contractor shall perform HPC under Standard Methods (SM) 9215 using acceptable variants (e.g., 9215B, 9215D/R2A, 9215E). Contractor shall document media, incubation temperature, and duration for each sample; the selected method/media shall remain consistent throughout the period of performance for comparability of trends. 3.2 Certifications & Accreditation Contractor shall hold current state certification/accreditation explicitly listing HPC under SM 9215 for the place(s) of performance (e.g., MSDH Drinking Water Laboratory Certification in Mississippi; Florida DOH/NELAP in Florida); ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation covering HPC is preferred. Copies of certificates and scopes must be provided. 3.3 Sample Handling & Logistics Contractor shall provide sampling containers, labels, chain?of?custody (COC) forms, coolers, and transport ice/ice packs; maintain 0�10?�C during transport; prevent freezing. Contractor shall initiate HPC analysis within applicable program hold times and in no case exceed 24 hours from collection unless stricter state limits are applicable. 3.4 Turnaround & Reporting Standard reporting shall be provided within 48 hours of laboratory receipt. Per?sample reports must include sample ID/location, collection and receipt timestamps, method/media/incubation conditions, HPC result in CFU/mL, and QC/batch identifiers. Contractor shall flag and notify the COR for any sample exceeding 500 CFU/mL and provide interpretive notes consistent with EPA guidance. 3.5 Emergency/Surge Capability Contractor shall provide rapid response capability for urgent events (e.g., main breaks, disinfection upsets) and identify surge capacity (peak samples/day) to meet VA needs. 4. ACQUISITION PATHWAYS & MANDATORY SOURCES The Government anticipates competing this requirement via Open Market or GSA MAS SIN 541380 if available. Nothing in this RFI commits the Government to a particular path. 5. SMALL BUSINESS & VETERANS FIRST VA will consider the results of this market research to determine small business set?asides and/or the use of Veterans First authorities. SDVOSB/VOSB respondents should indicate VetCert verification status. Any decision to set aside or use VAAR Subpart 819.70 sole?source authorities (?$5M) will be made at the Government�s discretion and in the best interest of the Government based on market research outcomes. 6. WHAT TO SUBMIT (Capability Statement � 10 pages max) A. Firm Information: Legal name, UEI, CAGE, business size/status (SB, SDVOSB, VOSB, HUBZone, WOSB), primary NAICS (541380) and any relevant NAICS. B. MAS Information (if applicable): GSA MAS contract number; confirmation of SIN 541380 listing; link to eLibrary T&Cs/price list. C. Certifications: Current state certification/accreditation scopes explicitly listing SM 9215 HPC (e.g., MSDH, FL DOH/NELAP) and ISO/IEC 17025 scope (if held). Attach certificates/scopes. D. Methods: Identify SM 9215 variant(s) used (B/D/R2A/E) and your approach to method/media consistency for trend comparability. E. Logistics & TAT: Confirm ability to meet hold?time limits (?24 h minimum; stricter limits prevail) and report within ?48 h; describe courier coverage, latest daily lab receipt times, and COC controls. F. QA/QC: Proficiency testing participation, batch QC practices, and LIMS/portal capabilities for electronic reporting. G. Past Performance: Healthcare water microbiology clients (VA/DoD/hospitals). Provide references (optional). H. Pricing (Non?binding for planning): Rough order?of?magnitude per?sample pricing; field collection fees; surge/expedite rates. 7. GOVERNMENT FURNISHED INFORMATION With any future solicitation, the Government may furnish sampling maps, historical HPC data for trend continuity, and site points of contact. (Not provided at the RFI stage.) 8. Instructions and Response Guidelines: Sources Sought responses are due by September 23, 2026 at 10:00 am (CST) via email to anthony.marion2.gov. All Questions shall be submitted by September 17, 2026 at 10:00 pm (CST) via email to anthony.marion2.gov. Telephone requests or inquires will not be accepted. Public Information will not be provided and shall be utilized to the full extent possible. This a New Requirement. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on Contracting Opportunities (https://beta.sam.gov/) website or GSA. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor these sites for additional information pertaining to this Sources Sought, or future RFP/RFQ. 9. DISCLAIMER This RFI is not a request for proposals or quotations. The Government will not reimburse costs incurred for responding. The Government reserves the right to use information provided to inform the acquisition strategy. If a solicitation is issued, it will be posted separately on SAM.gov.

title: Gas Cylinders - Remove, Transport, Dispose
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation that will be issued. Quotations are being requested, and separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1232SA26Q1502 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for ARS Pacific Basin Agricultural Research Center. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 541620, Environmental Consulting Services. The small business size standard is $19 mil This acquisition is set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Statement of Requirement The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), Pacific Basin Agricultural Research Center (PBARC), Hilo, Hawaii, requires contractor services to safely remove, characterize (if necessary), transport, and dispose of three (3) compressed gas cylinders with unknown contents (see Figure 1). The cylinders are legacy materials located in a USDA storage building and are no longer required for research operations. Note: The removable steel cylinder caps have become corroded and stuck, making them difficult to remove. Since shipping regulations require tank valves to be accessible, specialized hydraulic equipment may be needed to detach the caps and replace the valves safely. Because the identity and condition of the gases cannot be confirmed by the Government, the contractor shall provide all technical expertise necessary to safely identify (when required), package, transport, and dispose of the cylinders in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations.

description: 09/14/2026 **RFI added to attachments, Update WD, Update price sheet, Update visible version of PWS** This is a solicitation for High Reach Genie Services - FA600626Q0033. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This requirement is for standard commercial preventative maintenance inspections (annual and quarterly safety compliance checks) and unscheduled mechanical repair services for a fleet of eight (8) specialized aerial boom lifts, scissor lifts, and material handling tow tractors at Westover Air Reserve Base. Based on formal market surveillance, this procurement is set aside 100% for Small Business. A GSA MAS schedule was determined to be a non-viable option due to the critical mission requirement for a 24-hour localized on-site emergency response window, which is not available from national schedule vendors without incurring excessive, non-commercial travel surcharges. Offerors must conform with the complete PWS. Key technical parameters include: Broadened Technician Certifications: Technicians must hold active credentials meeting ANSI/IPAF standards for aerial lift platforms (Genie/JLG), or equivalent commercial mechanical certifications (forklift/automotive drivetrain) for material handling tow tractors (Toyota). Decoupled Emergency Response Timelines: Phase 1 (Notification to On-Site Diagnosis): Contractor technician must arrive on-site within 24 hours of receiving an emergency service call from the Maintenance Flight. Phase 2 (Diagnostics to Estimate Submission): Contractor must submit an itemized repair and parts estimate to the Contracting Officer within 24 business hours of completing the diagnostic visit. Phase 3 (Approval to Final Repair): Contractor must complete the physical repair work within 24 hours of receiving formal electronic approval from the Contracting Officer. Proprietary Parts Sourcing Exemption: For standard parts and commercial consumables, the contractor must supply three (3) competitive quotes. For proprietary Genie or JLG components, the contractor is exempt from the three-quote requirement and may supply a single manufacturer-authorized quote paired with current MSRP catalog listings. Future Equipment Phase-In: The fleet currently contains four active assets, with four additional assets (2 JLG lifts and 2 Toyota tow tractors) currently on order. Offerors will not charge the firm-fixed PM rate for on-order assets. The government will activate the corresponding CLINS (CLINs 0004, 1004, etc.) via administrative modification only once the new equipment is formally accepted. Addendum to RFO FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services: Quotes must be submitted electronically to the Contracting Officer via email at robert.stacy.1@us.af.mil no later than September 16, 2026, at 1200 hours EST. The submission must consist of two separate volumes: Sub-Factor 1: Personnel Qualifications. Submit active training records, ANSI/IPAF credentials, or equivalent heavy machinery/drivetrain repair certifications proving technicians are qualified to perform work on commercial-grade boom lifts, scissor lifts, and industrial tow tractors. Sub-Factor 2: Responsive Deployment Plan. Provide a narrative detailing the technician deployment workflow, showing how the contractor will meet the strict 24-hour emergency on-site diagnostic requirement at Westover ARB. Completed Section 2.0 Pricing Tables for the Base Year and all Option Years. All prices must be rounded to the nearest cent. Addendum to RFO FAR 52.212-2, Evaluation � Commercial Products and Commercial Services: The Government will award a single, Firm-Fixed-Price contract to the responsible offeror whose quote represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated using a two-step process: Each quote will be evaluated on a Pass/Fail basis against the following technical factors: Factor 1: Personnel Qualifications. Acceptable only if the contractor submits valid ANSI/IPAF, Genie/JLG OEM, or equivalent heavy equipment/automotive drivetrain certifications for all proposed service technicians. Factor 2: Responsive Deployment Plan. Acceptable only if the contractor�s plan demonstrates a clear, logical, and dependable process to get a qualified technician on-site at Westover ARB within 24 hours of notification. Of those quotes determined to be Technically Acceptable, the contract will be awarded to the offeror with the lowest cumulative total price for the Base Year and all Option Years (excluding the future equipment phase-in pool which is preset by the Government). The following RFO FAR and R-DFARS clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference: RFO FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Aug 2026). RFO FAR 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions � Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Aug 2026). RFO FAR 52.217-9, Option to Extend the Term of the Contract (Aug 2026) � Within 30 Days of contract expiration. R-DFARS 252.204-7003, Control of Government Personnel Work Product (Aug 2026). R-DFARS 252.232-7003, Electronic Submission of Payment Requests and Receiving Reports (Aug 2026).

title: Pre-solicitation Notice with Intent to Sole Source � Sportsmobile Texas, Inc.
description: DESCRIPTION The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Farm Production and Conservation (FPAC) Business Center, on behalf of the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS), intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to Sportsmobile, Inc., located at 9805 Gray Blvd #B, Austin TX 78758-5411. This procurement is conducted in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 12.102(b) for the acquisition of commercial services. The USDA requires upfit services for a Government Furnished 2024 Mercedes Benz Sprinter 170" Extended Cargo Van. Background and Requirement Description: This acquisition is for the design, fabrication, and installation of a custom interior upfit for one Government-furnished 2024 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 170" Extended 2500 Cargo Van. The completed upfit will convert the vehicle into a specialized Mobile Engineering Field Laboratory and Quality Assurance Command Center for USDA-FPAC-NRCS-Texas watershed infrastructure projects.and servicing functions, and manage the active Farm Loan Programs (FLP) portfolio. The required upfit includes insulation, a cab partition/bulkhead with walkthrough opening, heavy-duty commercial flooring, integrated workstation and cabinetry, specialized shelving and soil sample storage, auxiliary power and climate control systems, galley and water systems, durable interior finishes, and safety features. The upfit must preserve safe vehicle handling and weight distribution due to the Sprinter van�s extended rear overhang and 2500 GVWR. The completed vehicle will enable USDA-NRCS engineers, watershed construction project managers, and inspectors to conduct field-based soil testing, maintain sample integrity, secure sensitive equipment, review project documentation, and perform real-time quality assurance activities at remote watershed construction sites. Sole Source Justification: The Government�s requirement is for a highly specialized custom upfit of a government furnished 2024 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 170" Extended 2500 Cargo Van into a mobile engineering field laboratory for USDA-FPAC-NRCS-Texas watershed infrastructure projects. This requirement is not a standard van interior build or general recreational vehicle conversion. The upfit must support field engineering, soil sample testing, secure transport of sensitive equipment, and real-time quality assurance functions at remote watershed construction sites. Sportsmobile Texas, Inc. demonstrated the technical expertise, engineering capability, and relevant industry experience to perform the custom design, fabrication, and installation required for this project. Market research showed that Sportsmobile Texas, Inc. can meet the Government�s specific technical requirements, including platform-specific weight distribution, custom laboratory layout, secure storage for field testing equipment and soil samples, a heavy-duty walkthrough cab partition, auxiliary power systems, water systems, durable field-use materials, and safety-focused installation. The requirement is unique because it combines vehicle upfitting, mobile laboratory functionality, secure transport of sensitive engineering equipment, rugged field use, and platform-specific design constraints for a government furnished 2024 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 170" Extended 2500 Cargo Van. Other vendors reviewed during market research did not demonstrate the same ability to meet the complete integrated requirement without compromising the Government�s need for safety, functionality, storage security, weight distribution, or field laboratory capability. Instructions to Industry: This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. All responsible sources who believe they can provide the capability may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which may be considered by the agency. Interested vendors must demonstrate how they can provide the required services and demonstrate their capability to meet the complete integrated requirement without compromising the Government�s need for safety, functionality, storage security, weight distribution, or field laboratory capability. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to the Contract Specialist no later than September 23, 2026, at 12:00 PM EST.

description: This is a notice of intent to award a sole source contract. Pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulations FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i). The Embassy of the United States of America in Lome, Togo has a requirement to replace the chiller coils at the Embassy building. The Embassy requires the immediate removal of existing compromised and corroded HVAC chiller coils and the installation of new, direct-fit replacement coils on the facility�s chiller systems. The scope of this project involves the procurement, delivery, and installation of commercial-grade chiller coils to restore the facility's HVAC cooling capacity and efficiency. The Embassy of the United States Lome, Department of State intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract on a sole-source basis to: Johnson Controls Industries � YORK & SABROE Service 14 Rue de Bel Air - 44470 - Carquefou FRANCE Phone number: +33.240.30.63.70 - +33.611.95.75.71 The scope of this acquisition requires from the contractor to provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, and transportation necessary to perform the following core tasks: Field verify existing dimensions, configurations, and performance specifications of the current chiller coils. Safely recover and dispose of existing refrigerants in accordance with EPA regulations. Demolish and remove the damaged or degraded cooling coils. Supply and install new, heavy-duty replacement coils matching or exceeding original equipment manufacturer (OEM) performance standards. Reconnect all piping, controls, and electrical components. Perform pressure testing, vacuum pull-down, refrigerant charging, and comprehensive system startup testing to verify proper operation. The anticipated period of performance is three months Place of Performance: US Embassy Lome 4332 blvd Eyadema � Cit� OUA BP 852 Lome Togo Statutory Authority This procurement is being conducted in accordance with FAR Part 13, Simplified Acquisition Procedures. This contract action is for supplies and services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.106-1(b)(1)(i), "Soliciting from a Single Source" for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold. Justification for Single Source Johnson Controls (JCI) is uniquely qualified and is the only known source capable of fulfilling this requirement because the rusted coils are part of an existing JCI / York Air Handling Unit (AHU) or Chiller. Replacing them with third-party, non-OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) coils introduces a high risk of improper alignment, sizing mismatches, and compromised structural integrity. The existing air handling infrastructure relies on proprietary dimensions and specific engineering design thresholds unique to Johnson Controls. Utilizing an aftermarket coil would modify the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) configuration, altering the precise static pressure drop, air velocity profiles, and thermal performance parameters engineered by JCI. The vendor possesses proprietary rights, data software, or manufacturing drawings essential to completing the work. Capability Statements and Responses THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES; AND NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE. title: High Reach Genie Services
description: This is a solicitation for High Reach Genie Services - FA600626Q0033. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This requirement is for standard commercial preventative maintenance inspections (annual and quarterly safety compliance checks) and unscheduled mechanical repair services for a fleet of eight (8) specialized aerial boom lifts, scissor lifts, and material handling tow tractors at Westover Air Reserve Base. Based on formal market surveillance, this procurement is set aside 100% for Small Business. A GSA MAS schedule was determined to be a non-viable option due to the critical mission requirement for a 24-hour localized on-site emergency response window, which is not available from national schedule vendors without incurring excessive, non-commercial travel surcharges. Offerors must conform with the complete PWS. Key technical parameters include: Broadened Technician Certifications: Technicians must hold active credentials meeting ANSI/IPAF standards for aerial lift platforms (Genie/JLG), or equivalent commercial mechanical certifications (forklift/automotive drivetrain) for material handling tow tractors (Toyota). Decoupled Emergency Response Timelines: Phase 1 (Notification to On-Site Diagnosis): Contractor technician must arrive on-site within 24 hours of receiving an emergency service call from the Maintenance Flight. Phase 2 (Diagnostics to Estimate Submission): Contractor must submit an itemized repair and parts estimate to the Contracting Officer within 24 business hours of completing the diagnostic visit. Phase 3 (Approval to Final Repair): Contractor must complete the physical repair work within 24 hours of receiving formal electronic approval from the Contracting Officer. Proprietary Parts Sourcing Exemption: For standard parts and commercial consumables, the contractor must supply three (3) competitive quotes. For proprietary Genie or JLG components, the contractor is exempt from the three-quote requirement and may supply a single manufacturer-authorized quote paired with current MSRP catalog listings. Future Equipment Phase-In: The fleet currently contains four active assets, with four additional assets (2 JLG lifts and 2 Toyota tow tractors) currently on order. Offerors will not charge the firm-fixed PM rate for on-order assets. The government will activate the corresponding CLINS (CLINs 0004, 1004, etc.) via administrative modification only once the new equipment is formally accepted. Addendum to RFO FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services: Quotes must be submitted electronically to the Contracting Officer via email at robert.stacy.1@us.af.mil no later than September 16, 2026, at 1200 hours EST. The submission must consist of two separate volumes: Sub-Factor 1: Personnel Qualifications. Submit active training records, ANSI/IPAF credentials, or equivalent heavy machinery/drivetrain repair certifications proving technicians are qualified to perform work on commercial-grade boom lifts, scissor lifts, and industrial tow tractors. Sub-Factor 2: Responsive Deployment Plan. Provide a narrative detailing the technician deployment workflow, showing how the contractor will meet the strict 24-hour emergency on-site diagnostic requirement at Westover ARB. Completed Section 2.0 Pricing Tables for the Base Year and all Option Years. All prices must be rounded to the nearest cent. Addendum to RFO FAR 52.212-2, Evaluation � Commercial Products and Commercial Services: The Government will award a single, Firm-Fixed-Price contract to the responsible offeror whose quote represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated using a two-step process: Each quote will be evaluated on a Pass/Fail basis against the following technical factors: Factor 1: Personnel Qualifications. Acceptable only if the contractor submits valid ANSI/IPAF, Genie/JLG OEM, or equivalent heavy equipment/automotive drivetrain certifications for all proposed service technicians. Factor 2: Responsive Deployment Plan. Acceptable only if the contractor�s plan demonstrates a clear, logical, and dependable process to get a qualified technician on-site at Westover ARB within 24 hours of notification. Of those quotes determined to be Technically Acceptable, the contract will be awarded to the offeror with the lowest cumulative total price for the Base Year and all Option Years (excluding the future equipment phase-in pool which is preset by the Government). The following RFO FAR and R-DFARS clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference: RFO FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Aug 2026). RFO FAR 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions � Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Aug 2026). RFO FAR 52.217-9, Option to Extend the Term of the Contract (Aug 2026) � Within 30 Days of contract expiration. R-DFARS 252.204-7003, Control of Government Personnel Work Product (Aug 2026). R-DFARS 252.232-7003, Electronic Submission of Payment Requests and Receiving Reports (Aug 2026).

description: DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. This Sources Sought is a market research tool being used to determine potential and eligible business firms that are capable of providing the services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a Request for Proposal. The existing contract was previously competed, with two offers received. Nevertheless, the Government would like to ensure that there is adequate competition for this procurement. Additionally, the results of this sources sought will also be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. All interested large and small businesses are encouraged to respond with a capability statement, but only those businesses or teaming arrangements that are considered small under NAICS 541330-1 will be considered for small business set-aside decisions. INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) at Patuxent River, MD announces its intention to procure, on a competitive basis services to provide Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C6ISR) integration and installation; systems engineering support; In-Service Engineering Agent (ISEA); and logistics support to Mission Systems programs, systems, and technological areas within the SAIW project portfolio. Further details are provided in the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS)/Statement of Work (SOW) attached to this synopsis (Attachment 1). The services are currently being performed by The MIL Corporation of Bowie, MD under N00421-24-D-0002. The current contract is Cost-Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) containing both performance-based Completion CLINs and Level-of-Effort (LOE) CLINs. This contract is due to expire 14-FEB-2029. Although the current Period of Performance (PoP) of this requirement is scheduled to end Q2 FY2029, the estimated exhaustion date is now within Q1 FY2028. PROGRAM BACKGROUND As the organic Lead Systems Integrator� (oLSI�) for the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) operates under a product-based business model whereby NAWCAD WOLF civilians lead and manage the execution of the requirements with combined Government-Industry teams. Using this oLSI� approach, the Government maintains control of intellectual property and data rights, enabling WOLF to rapidly adapt solutions to the dynamic needs of the warfighter. The NAWCAD WOLF Ship & Air Integrated Warfare (SAIW) Division is the oLSI� providing design, procurement, integration, testing, and training of Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence (C4I) electronic systems that meet the requirements of the United States Navy operating forces. The SAIW Division, operating under the oLSI� model, has requirements for services to provide Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance integration and installation (C6ISR); systems engineering support; In-Service Engineering Agent; and logistics support to Mission Systems programs, systems, and technological areas within the SAIW project portfolio. REQUIREMENTS Please review Attachment 1, Draft PWS/SOW and Attachment 2, Draft Hours. If your company has any questions about the PWS/SOW, Draft Hours, or any areas that may need further explanation, please also identify those in the response. The labor categories anticipated to execute the contemplated effort are included in Attachment 2, Draft Hours. Since the resultant contract will be a cost-type effort, the successful awardee will also be required to have a Government approved accounting system upon award. All Contractors that propose must either have or be able to obtain a TOP SECRET facility clearance. A DD Form 254 Contract Security Classification Specification shall apply to this requirement and the prime contractor shall have a �Top Secret� Facility Clearance and a �Secret� Safeguarding Clearance. ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this requirement is 541330-1 Engineering Services with a Small Business Size standard of $47 Million. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. The Product Service Code (PSC) for this effort will be K058: Modification of Equipment - Communication, Detection, and Coherent Radiation Equipment PLACE OF PERFORMANCE % On-Site Government % Off-Site Contractor WOLF St. Ingioes, MD 100% 22% 78% ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE The requirement is anticipated to be a Single Award, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA IDIQ) contract with Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) Level of Effort (LOE)/Term Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) for a portion of labor, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) CLINs for the remaining labor, and cost reimbursable CLINs for Other Direct Costs (ODCs). The proposed contract is anticipated to include tasking and labor categories that are subject to the Service Contract Act. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE It is anticipated that the resultant contract is estimated to begin in Q1 FY2028 and will have a five-year ordering period It is anticipated performance will commence approximately in December 2027. The estimated manhours hours by CLIN type are as follows: For the FFP CLINs: 272,910 manhours (for estimating purposes only, based on projections from historical data.) For the CPAF CLINs: 892,097 manhours SUBMITTAL INFORMATION It is requested that interested businesses submit to the contracting office a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 15 pages in length, single spaced, 12 point font minimum) demonstrating the ability to perform the effort listed in the attached Draft PWS/SOW, Attachment 1. This documentation must address, at a minimum, the following: Title of the PWS/SOW to which you are responding; Company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), CAGE code, DUNS number, and a statement regarding current small/large business status; Respondents to this notice must also indicate whether they qualify as a Small, Small Disadvantaged, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Women-Owned, 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business (HUB) Zone, or Veteran Owned Small Business concern; If a small business, provide an explanation of your company's ability or your company�s ability combined with a similarly situated entity�s ability to perform at least 50% of the tasking described in this PWS/SOW; Resources available such as corporate management and currently employed personnel to be assigned to tasks under this effort to include professional qualifications, specific experience of such personnel, and the ability to have personnel located at the city specified; Management approach to staffing this effort with qualified personnel; Statement regarding capability to obtain the required industrial security clearances for personnel; Company's ability to meet the requirements in the Facility and Safeguarding requirements; Company's ability to begin performance upon contract award; Company's ability to manage a team of subcontractors, including a list of contracts and teaming arrangements; Prior/current corporate experience performing efforts of similar size and scope within the last three years, including contract number, organization supported, indication of whether as a prime or subcontract

title: FEMA Region VI: IT Equipment
description: The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, has identified a need to replace end-of-life laptops and acquire various IT peripheral equipment necessary to maintain operational capability, cybersecurity compliance, and workforce productivity. The purpose of this Request for Quotation is to solicit quotations from authorized resellers and distributors for the supply of the brand-name equipment identified in the schedule of supplies, including Dell, Cisco, Samsung, Sharp, Crestron, and associated peripheral equipment. This RFQ is issued as an open market total small business set-aside under NAICS 541519, Other Computer Related Services, with a small business size standard of 150 employees. Award will be made to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable responsible small business quoter whose quotation conforms to all requirements of this RFQ. Offerors shall identify the exact brand name, model number, part number, and specifications of each item proposed. All quoted items must match the specified brand name, model number, part number, and configuration exactly. Substitutions, alternatives, or deviations will not be accepted unless expressly authorized in writing by the Contracting Officer. Offerors must be authorized resellers or distributors of the specified brands. The Government reserves the right to verify reseller or distributor authorization directly with the original equipment manufacturer. Offerors shall provide a letter or certificate of authorization upon request. For purposes of this requirement, the prime quoter may satisfy the authorized reseller/distributor requirement by providing documentation demonstrating that the specified products will be procured through an OEM-authorized distributor or reseller channel. The prime quoter is not required to hold direct reseller/distributor authorization from each OEM, provided the documentation submitted is sufficient for the Government to verify the authorized source and channel eligibility of the quoted products. The Government seeks quotes with a total price less than $370,000.00. Quoters should not interpret this figure as a ceiling or as a floor on offers. This information is provided as a courtesy to prospective offerors. The Government may select an offer for award with a price below, at, or exceeding this figure if it finds the quotation technically acceptable, price is reasonable, and funds are available. Delivery shall be FOB Destination. Equipment shall be delivered within 70 calendar days after receipt of order. Shipment tracking information and delivery confirmation shall be provided upon request. All questions and quotations shall be submitted by email to the Contracting Officer, Destiny Dyson, at Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov. Phone calls will not be accepted. Quoters shall use the Open Market RFQ 70FBR626Q00000044 - FEMA Region VI IT Equipment identifier in all questions, correspondence, and quotation submissions. Questions regarding this RFQ are due no later than September 17, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Questions shall be submitted by email to the Contracting Officer, Destiny Dyson, at Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov. Questions submitted after the deadline may not be answered. Oral questions or responses are not binding. Only written responses issued by the Contracting Officer are binding on the Government. Quotations are due no later than September 23, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Quotations shall be submitted by email to the Contracting Officer, Destiny Dyson, at Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov. Quotations submitted by any other method may not be considered unless expressly authorized by the Contracting Officer. Quoters are responsible for ensuring that quotations are received by the Contracting Officer by the due date and time. Late quotations may not be considered in accordance with applicable procedures. For Dell laptop CLINs, offerors shall quote the exact configurations identified in the applicable attached manufacturer configuration sheets, including the listed hardware specifications and warranty/support packages, unless otherwise expressly authorized in writing by the Contracting Officer. Partial deliveries are permitted, provided all required items are delivered no later than 70 calendar days after receipt of order. Partial delivery does not change the required final delivery date and does not constitute final acceptance of the order unless accepted by the Government. Manufacturer lead-time delays or backorders do not waive the required delivery date unless the Contracting Officer issues a written modification. Quoters should only quote items they reasonably expect to deliver within the required delivery period. Clarification for CLIN 0001 and CLIN 0004: CLIN 0001 and CLIN 0004 require the same Dell Pro Max 16 configuration/specifications. title: Control System Replacement for Stamford Hurricane Barrier, Stamford, CT
description: Notice of Intent for Stamford Hurricane Barrier � Control Systems Replacement � Rockwell Automation Under the authority of RFO 6.103-1, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers intends to require, on a sole source basis, the purchase and installation of the control system hardware and proprietary programming software to Rockwell Automation for the upcoming Stamford Hurricane Barrier Control System Replacement project. The Stamford Hurricane Barrier is a critical life-safety public infrastructure asset providing immediate flood and storm protection to the region. Specifying Rockwell Automation is essential to the Government's requirement for the following reasons: USACE New England District (NAE) possesses exclusive, in-house engineering expertise in Rockwell Automation platforms. By standardizing Rockwell, NAE�s in-house staff will perform the system programming, installation oversight, and final commissioning at a direct labor cost of $0 to the contract. Procuring a non-Rockwell system would force the Government to procure external, specialized contractor integration services and purchase redundant diagnostic hardware/software and retraining of NAE personnel. The barrier must be activated at a moment's notice during severe weather events. Currently, NAE�s in-house Rockwell experts provide immediate, 24/7 emergency troubleshooting. Utilizing a different platform would render the Government entirely dependent on external contractors for emergency support, introducing an unacceptable delay in emergency response times during critical storm events. Submission of Capabilities: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT, NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR A SOLICITATION. A solicitation will be issued at a later date. However, any firm that believes it can provide an alternative control system platform that meets the technical requirements of the Stamford Hurricane Barrier AND can demonstrate how doing so would not result in a substantial duplication of cost or an unacceptable delay in emergency response for the Government may submit a capability statement. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. It is a market research tool being used to determine the availability of other qualified sources that can meet the requirements identified above and inherent with the referenced Stamford Hurricane Barrier Control Systems Replacement. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources because of this notice of intent. All responses received within 15 days of the posting of this notice of intent will be considered by the Government. title: BEAMERS Industry Day Announcement
description: INDUSTRY DAY: DARPA will host an Industry Day in support of Beam-Space Analog Processing for Multifunctional Enhanced RF Systems (BEAMERS) program on September 30, 2026, located at the Strategic Analysis, Inc. Executive Conference Center (ECC), 4075 Wilson Blvd, Suite 300, Arlington, VA 22203 from 8:00am to 5:00pm ET. This event will be conducted in two parts: a government presentation portion at the SECRET level, which will comprise most of the event, and an Industry Showcase Poster Session portion at the Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) level. Both portions exclusively require advanced registration. The purpose of this event is to provide information on the BEAMERS program; promote additional discussion on this topic; address questions; and provide a forum for interested organizations to present their capabilities for teaming opportunities. PROGRAM OBJECTIVE AND DESCRIPTION: DARPA�s Strategic Technology Office invites interested organizations to attend an industry engagement for BEAMERS, an ambitious new program focused on wideband, staring electronic-support systems. Electronic support cuts across many operational needs, platforms, and environments. Warning, situational awareness, sensing, and related missions impose different requirements for coverage, sensitivity, latency, dynamic range, size, weight, power, and processing. Staring architectures make a large amount of information available continuously. A successful system cannot assume that every beam, frequency channel, and polarization output will be digitized, transported, and processed at full fidelity. BEAMERS emphasizes architectures that maintain persistent awareness, organize and reduce the available analog information, recognize signals of potential interest, and route selected observations to digitization. Required expertise includes analog beamspace processing using lenses, gradient-index structures, phased-array-fed lenses, and related spatial-transform technologies; integrated radio frequency (RF) and microwave photonics; wideband channelization; event detection and information reduction; switching; and data movement. Organizations interested in performing as Prime and nontraditional technology providers are encouraged to attend, identify complementary capabilities, and consider teaming arrangements.
