title: Notice of Intent to Award Sole-Source BOA - Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC
description: 1.0 Description of Intent Army Contracting Command � Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA), intends to establish a sole-source, open-market Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) under the authority of 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 (Only One Reasonable Source�), with Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC (Maple Grove, MN). The proposed BOA will establish a 5-year framework (with a 6-month FAR 52.217-8) extension option) of pre-negotiated terms and pricing to support proprietary Zeiss metrology assets, with a total estimated capacity of $9,000,000.00. The primary NAICS code for this requirement is 811219 (Other Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance). 2.0 Scope of Services This agreement will provide critical Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) and associated proprietary metrology system (e.g., Surfcom) support. The scope covers baseline requirements for Tooele Army Depot (TEAD), McAlester Army Ammunition Plant (McAAP), and Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA), and is structured to allow any other Joint Munitions Command (JMC) or Army Materiel Command (AMC) installation to bilaterally on-ramp their proprietary Zeiss assets. Requirements issued under this BOA will include: Software Maintenance Agreements (SMAs): Proprietary CALYPSO and Surfcom MAP software version upgrades, bug fixes, CAD driver updates, and cyber security patches Preventative Maintenance and Calibration: Annual OEM-certified physical calibrations, to include writing back to the proprietary Zeiss Computer Aided Accuracy (CAA) volumetric error compensation matrix. Emergency Repair and OEM Parts: Factory-certified repair technicians and brand-new OEM replacement parts. Zeiss Care Plus: Optional, comprehensive extended hardware warranty packages. 3.0 Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the CMMs and Surfcom metrology systems and is the sole proprietary owner of the associated CALYPSO and Surfcom MAP metrology software. Zeiss does not license its software source code, nor does it share it�s proprietary diagnostic algorithms and CAA calibration matrices with third-party vendors. Consequently, only Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC or its factory-authorized technicians possess the proprietary data, diagnostic tools, and software keys required to perform these services without corrupting the equipment accuracy map or voiding current system warranties. 4.0 Response Instructions This is a Notice of Intent and is NOT a Request for Proposals (RFP) or a Request For Quote (RFQ); no solicitation is currently available. In accordance with FAR 5.207(c)(16)(ii), all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. Any interested vendor who believes they possess the capability and legal proprietary authorization to provide all described services (specifically including proprietary CALYPSO software updates and CAA error-matrix calibration) must submit their response via email to the Contracting Specialist, Dustin Sexton at dustin.p.sexton.civ@army.mil. Responses are due no later than 1:00pm CST on 23 September 2026 Capability statements are limited to 5 pages. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

IAW Attachment 1 - Statement of Work, The Livestock Arthropod Pest Research Unit (LAPRU) includes the Cattle Fever Tick Research Laboratory (CFTRL), which operates under biosecurity at the USDA Moore Air Base near Edinburg, Texas. This is a satellite facility of the Knipling-Bushland U.S. Livestock Insects Research Laboratory (KBUSLIRL) in Kerrville, Texas. Scientific endeavors at the CFTRL deliver technologies that the USDA Cattle Fever Tick Eradication Program can integrate to keep the U.S. free of cattle fever ticks in a sustainable manner. This ensures continued prosperity of the U.S. livestock industry. Unique assets at the CFTRL include cattle fever tick colonies, barns for studies with cattle that can be artificially infested with ticks, and pastures providing the ability to conduct studies with infested cattle resembling field conditions. However, modernization of the facilities is required to keep up with the expansion of the research program at the CFTRL that is underway to meet the expectations of the U.S. livestock industry and other stakeholders� groups. The current perimeter fence around pasture 7 is allowing wildlife onto the facility. This puts the facility at risk of losing our quarantine zones.

title: Notice of Intent to Award Sole-Source BOA - Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC
description: 1.0 Description of Intent Army Contracting Command � Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA), intends to establish a sole-source, open-market Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) under the authority of 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 (Only One Reasonable Source�), with Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC (Maple Grove, MN). The proposed BOA will establish a 5-year framework (with a 6-month FAR 52.217-8) extension option) of pre-negotiated terms and pricing to support proprietary Zeiss metrology assets, with a total estimated capacity of $9,000,000.00. The primary NAICS code for this requirement is 811219 (Other Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance). 2.0 Scope of Services This agreement will provide critical Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) and associated proprietary metrology system (e.g., Surfcom) support. The scope covers baseline requirements for Tooele Army Depot (TEAD), McAlester Army Ammunition Plant (McAAP), and Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA), and is structured to allow any other Joint Munitions Command (JMC), Army Materiel Command (AMC), Army Sustainment Command (ASC), and Tank-Automotive & Armaments Command (TACOM) CONUS installations to bilaterally on-ramp their proprietary Zeiss assets. Installations including but not limited to: -Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) - Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA) - Letterkenny Munitions Center (LEMC) - Joint Manufacturing and Technology Center (JMTC) to bilaterally on-ramp their proprietary Zeiss assets. Requirements issued under this BOA will include: Software Maintenance Agreements (SMAs): Proprietary CALYPSO and Surfcom MAP software version upgrades, bug fixes, CAD driver updates, and cyber security patches Preventative Maintenance and Calibration: Annual OEM-certified physical calibrations, to include writing back to the proprietary Zeiss Computer Aided Accuracy (CAA) volumetric error compensation matrix. Emergency Repair and OEM Parts: Factory-certified repair technicians and brand-new OEM replacement parts. Zeiss Care Plus: Optional, comprehensive extended hardware warranty packages. 3.0 Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the CMMs and Surfcom metrology systems and is the sole proprietary owner of the associated CALYPSO and Surfcom MAP metrology software. Zeiss does not license its software source code, nor does it share it�s proprietary diagnostic algorithms and CAA calibration matrices with third-party vendors. Consequently, only Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC or its factory-authorized technicians possess the proprietary data, diagnostic tools, and software keys required to perform these services without corrupting the equipment accuracy map or voiding current system warranties. 4.0 Response Instructions This is a Notice of Intent and is NOT a Request for Proposals (RFP) or a Request For Quote (RFQ); no solicitation is currently available. In accordance with FAR 5.207(c)(16)(ii), all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. Any interested vendor who believes they possess the capability and legal proprietary authorization to provide all described services (specifically including proprietary CALYPSO software updates and CAA error-matrix calibration) must submit their response via email to the Contracting Specialist, Dustin Sexton at dustin.p.sexton.civ@army.mil. Responses are due no later than 1:00pm CST on 23 September 2026 Capability statements are limited to 5 pages. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: Replace Perimeter Fence Pasture 7
description: IAW Attachment 1 - Statement of Work, The Livestock Arthropod Pest Research Unit (LAPRU) includes the Cattle Fever Tick Research Laboratory (CFTRL), which operates under biosecurity at the USDA Moore Air Base near Edinburg, Texas. This is a satellite facility of the Knipling-Bushland U.S. Livestock Insects Research Laboratory (KBUSLIRL) in Kerrville, Texas. Scientific endeavors at the CFTRL deliver technologies that the USDA Cattle Fever Tick Eradication Program can integrate to keep the U.S. free of cattle fever ticks in a sustainable manner. This ensures continued prosperity of the U.S. livestock industry. Unique assets at the CFTRL include cattle fever tick colonies, barns for studies with cattle that can be artificially infested with ticks, and pastures providing the ability to conduct studies with infested cattle resembling field conditions. However, modernization of the facilities is required to keep up with the expansion of the research program at the CFTRL that is underway to meet the expectations of the U.S. livestock industry and other stakeholders� groups. The current perimeter fence around pasture 7 is allowing wildlife onto the facility. This puts the facility at risk of losing our quarantine zones.

The resulting task orders will be negotiated Firm Fixed-Price for General Design and other related services. Should a task order require a T1 Background Investigation it will be specified. The primary purpose of the proposed contract is to provide A-E General Design and other related Services anywhere within the boundaries or assignments of Mississippi Valley Division. 2. PROJECT INFORMATION: A-E and related services are to be accomplished through individual Task Orders, which shall consist of the following comprehensive scope tasks and requirements: (a) Core Engineering, Design, and Project Documentation: The work will involve investigations, comparisons, data evaluations, analyses, designs, water quality analyses, technical writing, and drafting for: Engineering Documents: Preparing Design Documentation Reports (DDRs) geotechnical reports, feasibility studies, plans and specifications, Operation, Maintenance, Repair, Replacement, and Rehabilitation (OMRR&R) manuals, value engineering, or other technical engineering documents. Design, Modeling & Drafting: Civil design, hydraulic design, hydrologicanalysis, sediment transport, coastal engineering, structural design, geotechnical design, mechanical design, electrical design, architectural design, naval architecture, project management, building and civil information modeling (BIM/CIM), and CAD drafting. Engineering Support During Advertisement (EDA): Preparing amendments to the advertised plans and specifications and updating the BIM/CIM as warranted by comments received from prospective bidders. Engineering Support During Construction (EDC): Attending pre-construction conferences; responding to contractor requests for information (RFIs) and clarifications; reviewing submittals from the construction contractor; and performing monthly or bi-weekly site visits (or visits at critical times) to witness construction practices, observe site conditions, and document implementation of the design from the designer's perspective. Levee Safety & Structural Periodic Inspections: Performing detailed, systematic technical inspections and evaluations of the safety, stability, and operational adequacy of levees and civil works structures. Support Services: Surveying and the use of aerial mapping are required to support this work. (b) Required Disciplines & Professional Qualifications: The assembled team must demonstrate professional qualifications, education, training, licensing, certification, professional registration, overall relevant experience, and longevity within their disciplines and firm. Key design personnel must include: Engineering: Structural, Civil, Hydraulic (including hydrologic analysis, sediment transport, and coastal engineering), Geotechnical, Mechanical, Electrical, Corrosion, Environmental, and Cost Engineering. Scientific & Applied Fields: Hydrologists, Geologists, Architects, Naval Architects, and Surveyors. Geospatial & Technology Specialties: Geospatial Information Systems (GIS) Mapping and Analysis, Drafting via Computer-Aided Design (Autodesk), 3D Modeling CAD consisting of Building Information Modeling (BIM), and Civil Information Modeling (CIM), and professional Project Management. Marine Structures: Bulkheads, dolphins, fenders, guide walls, jetties, or shoreline protection. Highway & Infrastructure Work: Roads, ramps, bridges, utility relocations, and buildings (such as warehouses, pump houses, or offices related to the structures above). Risk Reduction & Environmental Projects: Flood risk management, hurricane and storm damage risk reduction projects, non-structural techniques (including elevation), freshwater and sediment diversion projects, environmental infrastructure projects, and other multi-purpose projects. Contract Package Development: Development of plans and specifications, Design-Build Requests for Proposals (RFPs), and real estate rights-of-way (ROW) drawings. Field Investigations & Testing: Hazard Toxic Radioactive Waste (HTRW) investigations; architectural treatments; landscaping; performing soil borings and soil testing to determine soil properties; and providing boring logs in accordance with USACE New Orleans District geotechnical criteria. title: B21 Low Observable/Radio Frequency Hangar (LO/RF) - OT Feasibility & Business Feedback
description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought (RFI) - B-21 Low Observable / Radio Frequency Hangar DISCLAIMER. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), or a commitment by the Government to write, issue, or award an agreement or contract. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All response costs will be borne solely by the interested party. PURPOSE. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. ACQUISITION STRATEGY & NON-FAR MODEL. Statutory Authority: This project will potentially be executed as a Progressive Design-Build (PDB), Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) or Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) project utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Non-FAR Environment: Prospective partners are advised that the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) does NOT apply to this procurement. The negotiated, bilateral Other Transaction Agreement will serve as the sole governing contract. Standard FAR clauses are inapplicable, though federal statutory constraints (such as federal fiscal law, criminal statutes, and general civil laws) remain fully applicable. Agreement Mechanics: PBD Procurement Process: Phase 1, Design & Pre-Construction Services, a design-builder will be selected through a qualifications-based selection (QBS) process. The government will then negotiate a fee for Phase 1 services. There is no requirement to submit price proposals or design concepts during the initial selection. Phase 2, Final Design & Construction, is executed via a bilateral modification to the OT Agreement upon successful negotiation of a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) at approximately 65% design maturity. The Agreement contains an "off-ramp" clause allowing the Government to retain the design and procure construction separately if GMP negotiations fail. DBtB Procurement Process: Solicitation and evaluation during Phase 1 focuses on the qualifications, past performance, and integrated Design-Build experience of each offeror. The Government is evaluating the team and not necessarily how the offeror will design the structure. The Phase 1 evaluation results in the selection of three of the most highly qualified, competitive teams to proceed to Phase 2. Phase 2, the Government will issue the final RFP exclusively to the down-selected teams. This RFP includes the validated, performance-based requirements, establishes the firm Construction Cost Limit (CCL), and clearly defines the basic scope. Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) Procurement Process: Early involvement, separate contracts, guaranteed maximum price and collaborative delivery. PROJECT OVERVIEW & SCOPE. Title: B-21 Low Observable / Radio Frequency Hangar Location: Dyess Air Force Base, Texas Scope: Construct a new 95,529 sq. ft. Low Observable Corrosion Control Hangar (LO) and a Radio Frequency Facility (RF) for the new B-21 weapons system. The project demands a highly collaborative and iterative design process to manage complexity and a critical schedule. Target Price Range (TPR): The Government has established The Government's Target Price Estimate for construction is between $280,000,000 and $300,000,000. Projected Award Date: The Government targets the formal award of the Agreement Phase 1 (Design and Preconstruction Services) on or about July 2027. Current Design is at 100%. The Government is willing to revert to a 35% design, allowing the awardee and designer the ability to collaborate during an OTA procurement process. Period of Performance (POP): The projected construction timeline is approximately 1217 calendar days following the execution of the Phase 2 Construction modification. Product Service Code (PSC): Y1BG (Construction of Electronic and Communications Facilities). NAICS Code: 236220 (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction). INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGIES & FEEDBACK AREAS. In accordance with Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC) Design Instruction #3, the Government is seeking commercial industry feedback regarding the feasibility and market capacity for the following innovative methods: Modular and Off-Site Prefabrication: Fabricating large sections of the facility or complex mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems in factory-controlled environments to compress the construction schedule. 3D Printing: Utilizing large-scale 3D printing for secondary building components, non-load-bearing walls, or perimeter security fencing. Advanced Materials: Incorporating self-healing concrete to reduce lifecycle maintenance and maximize structural integrity, or utilizing high-performance insulation (e.g., aerogels or vacuum-insulated panels) to meet high-performance building standards. Submissions: Submit your capabilities statement and Market Intelligence response (attachment) via email toThomas Howard at Thomas.W.Howard@usace.army.mil and Nicholas Johnston at Nicholas.I.Johnston@usace.army.mil no later than Wednesday, September 23st, 2026 at 2:00 PM CDT (21:00 UTC). Use email subject: "Sources Sought Response: B21 Low Observable/Radio Frequency Hangar (LO/RF) Market Intel - [Your Firm Name]". File Naming Convention: Market Intel_B21 LO/RF_[FIRM NAME]

title: Wideband Remote Monitoring Sensor (WRMS) Enhancement and Sustainment (E&S)
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of small and large businesses to provide the required products and/or services. The WRMS E&S requirement falls under Project Officer Wideband Control as part of its mission to acquire and install state-of-the-art strategic satellite network control and planning systems for use with the Defense Satellite Communications System and Wideband Global Satellite Communications (WGS), and to provide satellite monitoring in either synchronized Spectrum Information Gathering or In-beam monitoring modes. At its most basic level, the primary function of WRMS is to aid the user with the identification and resolution of anomalies detected by the system. Anomalies are presented to the user through the comparison of planned versus actual radio frequency measurement data. The current contract, now in its last year of execution, provided a spectrum characterization and analysis software from the ground-up coding in micro-services that provided a Government-owned custom software that implements a hardware agnostic interface, all targeted to support the WGS-11 satellite while being able to support all prior WGS satellites. This software and hardware solution is integrated with all current Wideband Control interface subsystems and maintains current performance specifications. The desired end-result of this forthcoming contract is to sustain this fielded version of WRMS, WRMS version release 3 (WRMS v3.x), and to provide enhancements based on feedback from the users as well as to continue addressing current and new software backlog items. title: Labeling Pilot for FDF Country of Origin, API Country of Origin, and KSM Country of Origin for Pharmaceutical Products
description: 1. Purpose The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support Medical Supply Chain is conducting market research to identify U.S. or international pharmaceutical manufacturers that are willing to participate in a labeling pilot program. The pilot seeks to explore voluntary inclusion of additional product labeling data for Pharmaceutical Products identifying: Country of origin for the Finished Dose Form (FDF) Country of origin for each Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) Country of origin for each Key starting material (KSM) necessary for the production of each API Given the amount of information requested, inclusion of a QR code or link to additional information, or other methods of making the information accessible, could be considered If the country of origin of the API or KSM can vary by lot produced, DLA would be interested in the information specific to the labeled lot and to any previously produced lots This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, and responses do not commit the Government to any future acquisition or requirement. 2. Background DLA Troop Support Medical is evaluating methods to improve supply chain transparency, enhance traceability, and strengthen operational readiness by increasing visibility into the sourcing of pharmaceutical ingredients. Understanding FDF, API, and KSM origins helps support contingency planning, risk modeling, and alignment with emerging regulatory and strategic sourcing initiatives. The agency is exploring the feasibility of obtaining this information directly from manufacturers through voluntary labeling enhancements on packaging, shipping containers, or supplemental documentation. 3. Scope of Pilot The proposed labeling pilot will focus on a selected subset of generic pharmaceutical products purchased by DLA Troop Support Medical. Participating manufacturers may be asked to provide: API country of manufacture API country of origin (if different) Country of origin for the Finished Dose Form (FDF) Country of origin for each Key starting material (KSM) necessary for the production of each API If the country of origin of the API or KSM can vary by lot produced, DLA would be interested in the information specific to the labeled lot and to any previously produced lots Placement of this information on external packaging, product containers, or accompanying supply chain documentation Given the amount of information requested, inclusion of a QR code or link to additional information, or other methods of making the information accessible, could be considered Estimated production or administrative impact associated with adding these data elements DLA seeks to understand both operational feasibility and industry readiness. 4. Requested Information from Respondents Interested manufacturers are invited to submit a written response addressing the following: A. Company name, CAGE code, point of contact information B. Description of the pharmaceutical products you manufacture that are supplied or could be supplied to DLA C. Willingness to participate in a voluntary labeling or data?sharing pilot to include: Development of a labeling construct that contains all relevant sourcing information as outlined below. Obtaining approval of the labeling construct from the Food and Drug Administration. Producing labels with all required sourcing information and affixing them to products sold to the Department of War. D. Ability to provide the following information for each lot produced: API country of manufacture API country of origin (if different) Country of origin for the Finished Dose Form (FDF) Country of origin for each Key starting material (KSM) necessary for the production of each API If the country of origin of the API or KSM can vary by lot produced, DLA would be interested in the information specific to the labeled lot and to any previously produced lots Placement of this information on external packaging, product containers, or accompanying supply chain documentation Given the amount of information requested, inclusion of a QR code or link to additional information, or other methods of making the information accessible, could be considered Estimated production or administrative impact associated with adding these data elements E. Existing internal capabilities or systems that support API and KSM traceability and documentation F. Expected timeline and level of effort required to implement labeling modifications G. Any concerns, limitations, or cost impacts associated with participation H. Recommendations for structuring or scaling the pilot program 5. Submission Instructions Responses should be submitted via email in PDF or Word format to the DLA Troop Support Medical Supply Chain point of contact: Contracting Officer: Charles T. Reimer DLA Troop Support � Medical Supply Chain Email: Charles.Reimer@dla.mil Phone: 267-251-9370 (Cell)

title: Wideband Remote Monitoring Sensor (WRMS) Enhancement and Sustainment (E&S)
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of small and large businesses to provide the required products and/or services. The WRMS E&S requirement falls under Project Officer Wideband Control as part of its mission to acquire and install state-of-the-art strategic satellite network control and planning systems for use with the Defense Satellite Communications System and Wideband Global Satellite Communications (WGS), and to provide satellite monitoring in either synchronized Spectrum Information Gathering or In-beam monitoring modes. At its most basic level, the primary function of WRMS is to aid the user with the identification and resolution of anomalies detected by the system. Anomalies are presented to the user through the comparison of planned versus actual radio frequency measurement data. The current contract, now in its last year of execution, provided a spectrum characterization and analysis software from the ground-up coding in micro-services that provided a Government-owned custom software that implements a hardware agnostic interface, all targeted to support the WGS-11 satellite while being able to support all prior WGS satellites. This software and hardware solution is integrated with all current Wideband Control interface subsystems and maintains current performance specifications. The desired end-result of this forthcoming contract is to sustain this fielded version of WRMS, WRMS version release 3 (WRMS v3.x), and to provide enhancements based on feedback from the users as well as to continue addressing current and new software backlog items. Please see the attached draft Performance Work Statement for more information.
